deepdive.divline: INR131cr raised: INR65cr to films, INR33cr to music/digital rights, INR32.5cr to corporate purposes; cash reserves untouched as of Q2FY26; prioritizing IP-led growth in film and digital over TV

profile.entities: Balaji Telefilms Limited; ALTT; Marinating Films
profile.subseg: Digital OTT Apps; Television Serials; Motion Pictures
profile.themes: IP Monetization; Hybrid SVOD+AVOD Model; Astrology Tech App; Balaji Studio

bull_bear.body: INR131cr raised: INR65cr to films, INR33cr to music/digital rights, INR32.5cr to corporate purposes; cash reserves untouched as of Q2FY26; prioritizing IP-led growth in film and digital over TV
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: TV revenue pressure from broadcaster cost cuts; high SVOD churn (65-70%); delayed monetization of digital order book until FY27; regulatory risk to apps (past ALTT ban); reliance on presales for film profitability
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes rebuilding pipeline, strong presales, and digital transformation; tone is forward-looking with focus on FY27 inflection
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR117cr GST input credit and INR100cr brought-forward losses will eliminate tax payments for 4-5 years, effectively boosting net cash flow despite reported losses
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Digital: 13% of Q2 revenue, 11M active subs on Kutingg, 400M YouTube views; TV: 77% revenue, 131 hrs produced, 4 shows running, episodic revenue at INR24-25L/hr; Film: 10% revenue, 3 films in production (Vrusshabha, Bhoot Bangla, Vvan), 85-90% cost recovered via presales
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TV revenue decline due to end of legacy shows | Balaji Telefilms Limited | beneficiary | High | Film and digital order book offsets TV weakness; presales ensure film profitability |
| High SVOD churn and low ARPU | Netflix | loser | Medium | Balaji's B2B content licensing to Netflix reduces dependency on direct consumer monetization |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: TV: 30% direct variable margin at INR24-25L/hr revenue; Film: 100% profit margin post-presales (e.g., Bhoot Bangla fully presold); Digital: low incremental cost for AstroVani/Kutingg, monetization via ads/subs
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Expected upside from Q1FY27; Margin: Film margins to be high due to 85-90% presales; Order inflow: INR300cr B2B digital order book growing; Capex/commissioning: INR150-175cr for films, INR20-25cr for digital working capital
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR300cr in B2B digital content orders (Netflix: INR250cr+, Zee Studios: INR42cr, Amazon/Sony/Star: incremental)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Balaji Studio (independent creator ecosystem), AstroVani (astrology app), AI-generated content on Kutingg, expansion into regional OTT partnerships (ETV, Aha), music rights monetization
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Revenue declined due to the natural end of 3 long-running TV shows and delayed movie releases, but the company is rebuilding its pipeline with a strong order book in B2B digital and 4 presold films launching in FY27, positioning digital and film as future profit drivers.

meta.thesis: Revenue declined due to the natural end of 3 long-running TV shows and delayed movie releases, but the company is rebuilding its pipeline with a strong order book in B2B digital and 4 presold films launching in FY27, positioning digital and film as future profit drivers.
